Significant-Gravitas/AutoGPT: An open AI agent platform that automatically breaks a goal down into tasks. It can choose tools, run steps, and organize results on its own, so you can focus on what you want done without building the whole toolchain from scratch. You only need to give it a goal, and the execution can be self-hosted.
langgenius/dify: A platform for building agent workflows and RAG applications. You can connect multiple models, knowledge bases, and tools, arrange them in a visual flow, then put the result in the cloud or host it yourself as an application that can chat and carry out tasks. Finished applications can be opened directly by other people through a chat interface.
langflow-ai/langflow: Build and deploy AI agents and workflows with visual flows. Each node can be a model, a prompt, a tool, or a data source, and drawing connections forms a flow you can try and run right away. After a flow is saved, you can change the nodes without starting over.
langchain-ai/langchain: An engineering platform for developing agents, assembling models, tools, memory, and flows into reusable applications. It suits people who want to control each step in code, rather than relying on one large prompt, and who want to connect their own data and systems. It suits engineers who need to connect databases, APIs, and their own internal systems.
browser-use/browser-use: A Python library that lets an AI agent control a browser. It can open pages, click buttons, fill forms, and extract data on its own, turning browsing into actions an agent can complete without you writing selectors step by step. Steps such as logging into an admin backend and moving data across pages can be handed to it to try.
google-gemini/gemini-cli: An open-source agent that brings Gemini into the terminal. You can assign development work from the command line and have it read the project, suggest changes, and run commands without leaving the terminal you already use. After the edits, they can stay in the original repo, so you do not have to switch to another editor.
infiniflow/ragflow: An open-source engine that combines retrieval-augmented generation with agents. It splits documents, builds indexes, and retrieves sourced context when answering, so the large model does not have to answer from its own memory alone. When an answer is wrong, you can check it against the cited passages instead of looking only at the final sentence.
OpenHands/OpenHands: An agent that uses AI for software development. You can hand it a development task, and it will edit code, run commands, read test results, and keep fixing based on failures, rather than only emitting a suggested snippet. A failed test stays in the same round so it can keep editing until the tests pass.
bytedance/deer-flow: A long-horizon agent framework for research, coding, and creative work. Complex tasks are split and handed to sandboxes, memory, and sub-agents to handle separately, so one conversation does not have to remember every step from the start. Research, coding, and creative work can be split into different subtasks and run together.
ruvnet/ruflo: An agent harness for coordinating multiple agents, automated workflows, and conversational systems with memory. The focus is putting roles, tools, and state in the same execution environment so they can finish longer tasks together. State does not disappear when a new conversation starts, which is what longer workflows need.
FoundationAgents/MetaGPT: A multi-agent framework that organizes product, design, and engineering roles into a software team. You describe requirements in natural language, and they divide the work by role to produce designs and code, rather than having one chatbot do everything at once. Outputs are filed by role, so you can review only the design or only the code.
cline/cline: A coding agent that can write code on its own, with an IDE extension, an SDK, and a command-line interface. It can read a project, edit files, and run commands, which suits people who want to assign development work directly inside the editor. The same instructions can be reused in the editor or on the command line.
openinterpreter/openinterpreter: A coding agent aimed at open-source models that can write code and run commands on the local machine. You describe what you want in natural language, and it generates and runs programs on your machine, with files and the environment staying local. Generated programs run locally, and result files stay on your computer.
mem0ai/mem0: A memory layer for AI agents. Facts worth remembering in a conversation are extracted and stored, then retrieved in later conversations, so the agent does not treat you as a first meeting every time. When a new session starts, it can look up old facts so the user does not have to say them again.
Mintplex-Labs/anything-llm: A self-hostable, local-first workspace. Documents, conversations, and agents stay on your own machine or your own server, which suits people who want question answering over private data without handing the files over. Private files can stay only on your own server while you still ask questions about them.
microsoft/autogen: Microsoft's agent programming framework for orchestrating multiple AIs that can converse and use tools. You can define each agent's role and the functions it can call, then let them take turns discussing until the task is done. It suits workflows where several specialized roles review one another before a result is delivered.
crewAIInc/crewAI: Forms autonomous agents in different roles into a team that completes more complex tasks together. Each member has its own goal and tools, and the flow decides who goes first and who continues, rather than one agent doing everything. What you change is the division of roles, not one prompt that keeps getting longer.
aaif-goose/goose: An extensible AI agent that does more than suggest code: it can also install, run, edit, and test. It operates the development environment on the local machine according to your instructions, which suits people who want a terminal assistant that can actually do the work. Installing dependencies and running tests are things it does itself, not only producing a diff.
FlowiseAI/Flowise: Build AI agents and language-model flows by drag and drop. Nodes can connect models, memory, and tools, which suits people who want to try a flow graphically first. The repository is archived, but it is still a common visual starting point. The repository is archived, and it is now better suited as a teaching reference and a reference for older flows.
CherryHQ/cherry-studio: A desktop AI workspace that puts chat, autonomous agents, and a large set of assistants in one program. You can connect different model providers and use a local interface to manage conversations, tools, and common workflows. When you switch model providers, the conversations and the assistant list still stay on the local machine.
run-llama/llama_index: A document processing and retrieval platform for connecting data to AI applications that can query and take action. It loads documents, builds indexes, and retrieves, then hands the result to a model to answer or to an agent to continue. Process the documents first, then decide whether to do question answering or hand the work to an agent.
HKUDS/nanobot: A lightweight, self-hostable personal agent framework. It includes a web interface, tools, memory, and multi-agent workflows, which suits people who want to run a small assistant on their own machine without first deploying a full platform. If you want a small-scale assistant first, you do not have to deploy a large platform at the start.
zhayujie/CowAgent: An open-source personal AI assistant that can plan tasks and use tools and skills. It remembers conversations and knowledge, so later tasks can refer to what it learned before instead of starting from an empty context every time. Skills and knowledge accumulate, so you repeat the same instructions less often.
langchain-ai/langgraph: Orchestrate reliable agent flows with a graph. Nodes and edges can express branches, loops, and human confirmation, which suits tasks whose steps loop back, or that take a long time to finish, rather than a straight line of calls. Requiring a person to press confirm, or going back to try again after a failure, can both be drawn as a graph.
agno-agi/agno: A self-improving agent platform for building and running AI agents. You can define tools and knowledge so the agent accumulates experience after a run and takes fewer detours the next time it handles similar work. Once a similar job has been done, the next time it can follow the earlier approach.
666ghj/BettaFish: A multi-agent public-opinion analysis assistant, implemented from scratch. Several roles divide the work of collecting public discussion, organizing a timeline, and reconstructing the event, helping you judge how a topic spread rather than only returning a pile of links. It suits tracking how one public event developed, rather than writing a general chatbot.
stanfordnlp/dspy: Compose language models in code instead of handwritten prompts. You split a task into modules, and the framework optimizes the prompt for each step, which suits people who want to tune a flow systematically rather than trying prompts sentence by sentence. When the task changes, you change the modules instead of manually trying a new prompt each time.
continuedev/continue: An open-source coding agent that can read and write code and finish development tasks inside the editor. It sees the current project context and edits, explains, and runs according to your instructions, without you pasting the whole repository into a chat window. Instructions are aimed at the files you have open, which reduces pasting the wrong context.
OpenBMB/ChatDev: Uses multiple language-model agents to play a development team and collaborate on software design and implementation. Roles such as product, coding, and testing take turns handing off work, moving one requirement toward code you can read, rather than generating it all at once. One requirement runs through the whole small team before you see readable code.
openai/openai-agents-python: OpenAI's lightweight Python framework for orchestrating multi-agent workflows. You can define handoffs, tools, and guardrails so several agents divide the work, which suits people who want to write agents directly against the official interface. If you want to follow OpenAI's current agent interface, this is closer to the official one than older tutorial frameworks.
assafelovic/gpt-researcher: An autonomous research agent that can gather material on a topic and write a sourced research report. It plans what to look up, reads the results, and synthesizes them, rather than answering only from a few passages you pasted in. You only need to give it a topic, without first finding ten papers yourself and pasting them in.
huggingface/smolagents: Hugging Face's compact agent library. Agents mainly think and act by writing code, turning a step-by-step plan into an executable program, which suits people who want little abstraction and direct control over tool calls. When a step goes wrong, you can look back at the program it wrote instead of a vague piece of reasoning.
mastra-ai/mastra: A framework for building AI applications and agents in TypeScript. Workflows, tools, and model calls are organized in code, so they fit into an existing web or server project without standing up a separate Python service. A service that already uses TypeScript can connect directly, without opening a separate Python service.
microsoft/semantic-kernel: Microsoft's SDK for connecting large language models, plugins, and planning into an application. You define skills in code, then let the model decide when to call business functions you already have. Functions in existing C# or other programs can be registered as skills the model can call.
deepset-ai/haystack: Build production language-model and agent applications with modular pipelines. Retrieval, generation, and tools are replaceable components, so you can control the input and output of each step instead of hiding the whole chain in a black box. In production you can swap the retrieval or model component without rewriting the entire pipeline.
letta-ai/letta: A stateful agent platform, formerly MemGPT, focused on long-term memory. An agent can write important content into memory and read it back when needed, so a project can accumulate across many conversations. Open the same agent again a few days later, and it still remembers the key points it wrote down before.
modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk: The official Python SDK for the Model Context Protocol. You can use it to write tool servers that agents can call, or clients that connect to those tools, so different programs exchange capabilities in the same way. Tools you write can be called by other agents that support this protocol.
Skyvern-AI/skyvern: Uses AI to automate browser workflows such as filling forms, logging into admin backends, and moving data across several pages. It decides the next step from the page content, which suits sites that change often and flows that are hard to maintain with fixed scripts. After a site redesign, fixed selectors break easily, and this kind of flow is more stable.
yoheinakajima/babyagi: An early, well-known autonomous agent experiment. You give it a goal, and it keeps creating the next task, executing by priority, and turning the results into new tasks. The program itself is very short and mainly demonstrates this loop. It is now mostly read as a historical example, not a full-featured product.
camel-ai/camel: A multi-agent framework that uses role-play and conversation to make several agents collaborate. You can specify the stance of two or more roles and let them question each other and finish the task, rather than having one assistant answer in one direction. It suits trying multi-role debate and division of work before deciding whether to switch to a heavier framework.
pydantic/pydantic-ai: Build agents in Python with clear types. Inputs, tool parameters, and outputs can all be described with types, which makes it easier to connect different models and interfaces and reduces cases where the model returns a pile of text that does not match the structure. When model output does not match the type, it fails clearly so you can catch it.
openai/swarm: A lightweight multi-agent tutorial framework from OpenAI. It shows how to hand work from one agent to another, and the code is deliberately kept short, so it is for understanding handoffs rather than as a full production platform. OpenAI later released a newer agent SDK, and this one is kept as a lightweight demonstration.
AUTOMATIC1111/stable-diffusion-webui: A widely used Stable Diffusion web interface for generating and adjusting images from text on your own machine. You can install extensions, switch models, inpaint, and upscale without writing your own inference code. Models, extensions, and inpainting are all switched on the same page, and it is many people's local entry point for generating images.
Comfy-Org/ComfyUI: An interface and backend for building diffusion-model pipelines as node graphs. Each step, such as loading a model, the prompt, ControlNet, and the output, is a node, which suits image generation you need to repeat and whose flow you need to change. The same graph can be saved as a workflow and run again next time with a different prompt.
PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR: A lightweight OCR tool that can turn images and PDFs into structured text. It supports many languages and layouts, which suits extracting text from scans, screenshots, or tables without first training your own model. It can handle layout and tables, not only single lines of text.
opencv/opencv: An open-source computer vision library for reading images and video and for filters, features, and detection. Research and products both use it for low-level operations such as resizing, finding edges, and tracking objects, then pass the result to a higher-level model. When you write your own vision pipeline, reading and writing, geometry, and features usually go through it first.
tesseract-ocr/tesseract: A classic open-source optical character recognition engine that can extract text from images. It has a long history and many language packs, and it suits command-line use or embedding text recognition in other programs without necessarily calling a neural-network service. It can run without a graphics card, and it suits embedding in older systems for batch text recognition.
CompVis/stable-diffusion: The latent diffusion text-to-image model released by CompVis, and the base for a large number of later generation tools. You can generate images from a text description, and later web UIs, fine-tunes, and plugins mostly extended this direction. The paper and the weights are both here, so if you want to trace text-to-image back to its source, you start with this.
lllyasviel/Fooocus: Wraps Stable Diffusion into a simplified interface focused on prompts and image output. Many model and parameter choices are tucked away, so you mainly edit the sentence to generate an image without first understanding a whole node graph. If you want to tune fewer parameters and see an image sooner, it is easier to start with than a full node interface.
roboflow/supervision: A computer vision toolkit for handling detection results, annotation, and visualization. Boxes and classes returned by a model can be filtered, counted, and drawn on the frame here, so you can check whether a detection pipeline is usable. You can change the detection model and still keep the post-processing code for reuse.
upscayl/upscayl: A free desktop AI image upscaler for Linux, macOS, and Windows. You drag in a low-resolution image, and it uses a super-resolution model to enlarge it and fill in detail without you setting up a Python environment. You do not need to open a terminal: drag a photo into the desktop program and the upscale is done.
TencentARC/GFPGAN: A face restoration algorithm for real photographs, used to recover blurry or damaged faces. It tries to preserve identity while filling in facial detail, and it is commonly used to restore old photos and enhance low-resolution portraits. Old photos and low-resolution portraits are the main use, and landscape restoration is not its focus. The background outside the face is not the part it is responsible for restoring.
huggingface/pytorch-image-models: A large collection of PyTorch image backbone models, including training, evaluation, and pretrained weights. You can swap models such as ResNet and ViT through the same interface, for classification or as the backbone of other vision tasks. When you change backbones for an experiment, the training and evaluation scripts do not have to be rewritten each time.
xinntao/Real-ESRGAN: A practical image and video restoration model for upscaling and improving quality. It has corresponding models for real photographs and for anime, and it suits enlarging small images while reducing blur and compression artifacts. Photographs and anime need different weights, and the scale factor can be set separately. When the scale factor is too large, watch whether faces and text become distorted.
huggingface/diffusers: Hugging Face's diffusion model library for image, video, and audio generation in PyTorch. Loading a model, sampling, and attaching a scheduler all have ready-made flows, so you can put generation into your own program. Image, video, and audio generation can all be connected through the same loading method.
openai/CLIP: A model that places images and text in the same space and can judge how well a piece of text matches a picture. Image search, classification, and later generative models all use it to measure how close an image is to the sentence you described. For your own unlabeled image collection, you can search with a sentence in a zero-shot way.
lllyasviel/ControlNet: Controls a diffusion model with condition images such as edges, pose, and depth, so generation follows a specified structure. You can give it a line drawing or a skeleton, and the model generates according to that shape instead of freely following the text alone. Pose, line drawings, and depth can be used together, and the structure is more stable than text alone.
lovell/sharp: A high-performance Node.js image processing module that uses libvips for resizing and format conversion. Web services often use it to process uploaded images, and it uses less memory than decoding the whole image at once. After a website backend receives an uploaded image, thumbnails and format conversion are usually handed to it.
JaidedAI/EasyOCR: Ready-to-use optical character recognition that supports more than eighty languages and multiple writing systems. The call is simple, which suits projects that want to extract text from photos quickly without first compiling a traditional OCR engine. When a photo contains several writing systems, you do not have to install an engine for each language first.
invoke-ai/InvokeAI: A creation-oriented Stable Diffusion engine for generating and editing visual content. Besides text-to-image, it emphasizes the canvas, local edits, and the creative workflow, which suits people who want a full studio rather than only a prompt box. It is for staying on the canvas to edit the image, rather than having only a prompt input box.
nagadomi/waifu2x: Anime-style image super-resolution for enlarging images while reducing aliasing and noise. It is especially common for line art and illustrations, and it can enlarge small anime images more cleanly. Other models are a better fit for photograph super-resolution, and its strength is anime linework. When you enlarge an anime screenshot, the lines come out cleaner.
GraphiteEditor/Graphite: Community-developed 2D creative software that uses nodes for graphic design, digital drawing, and motion graphics. Tools and effects can be connected into a graph, which suits people who want an editor that is still in development and aimed at vector and procedural design. It is still in development, and it suits people who want to try node-based graphic design and keep using it.
black-forest-labs/flux: The official inference code for the Black Forest Labs FLUX.1 image model. You can use it to run FLUX text-to-image on your own machine, as an entry point to an image model a generation newer than early Stable Diffusion. It is the official inference entry point, and you can generate a comparison image with it before connecting your own pipeline.
junyanz/pytorch-CycleGAN-and-pix2pix: A PyTorch implementation of image-to-image translation, including CycleGAN and pix2pix. It can do translations such as style transfer, season change, and sketch-to-photo with paired or unpaired data. Use pix2pix when you have paired data, and use CycleGAN when you only have two sets of images in different styles.
danielgatis/rembg: A tool that uses AI to remove image backgrounds automatically. It can be used from the command line or as a library, separating a person, a product, or another subject from the background and outputting a transparent background for later compositing. Product shots and portraits can both be exported with a transparent background, then passed to compositing or an online-store layout. After background removal, it is best to check the hair and semi-transparent edges.
Sanster/IOPaint: An AI image inpainting tool that can remove objects or redraw a chosen region with text and a diffusion model. You paint over the part you do not want, and the model fills it in from the surrounding picture or a prompt, without manual clone stamping. Removing passersby and redrawing a region from text can both be done in the same tool.
sczhou/CodeFormer: A face restoration model that uses a codebook to recover damaged or low-resolution facial detail. You can trade off fidelity against restoration strength so a face is not restored into a completely different person. If restoration is too strong it changes the likeness, so you set the fidelity yourself. Low-resolution ID photos and old portraits are both common uses.
ImageMagick/ImageMagick: An image toolkit that handles more than two hundred formats and can convert, edit, and composite from the command line. Batch thumbnails, format conversion, adding text, and montages all use it, and it is the underlying tool in many automated flows. For scripts and server-side batch image processing, it is still the most common command-line tool.
lukas-blecher/LaTeX-OCR: Turns images of mathematical formulas into LaTeX code. Photograph or screenshot a formula and you get editable source, which suits organizing equations in notes, papers, and scans. Handwritten and printed formulas can both be tried, and complex layouts need further manual editing. The generated code should still be pasted back into a compiler to check.
CompVis/latent-diffusion: Research code for high-resolution latent diffusion models, and the predecessor implementation of Stable Diffusion. It demonstrates doing diffusion in a compressed space and then decoding into an image, an approach later text-to-image models carried on. If you want to understand why Stable Diffusion does diffusion in latent space, start with this code.
python-pillow/Pillow: A Python image processing library for opening files, resizing, drawing, and converting formats. Almost every Python image program reads and writes files through it, then passes the pixels to a model or saves the result. Opening and saving files before and after a model is, in Python, usually done through it.
darktable-org/darktable: Open-source photo workflow and RAW development software for organizing and color-grading photos. You can manage a photo library and make non-destructive adjustments to RAW files, as an open-source alternative to commercial development software. Adjustments are written to a side record, so the original photo is not overwritten. Color-grading steps can be copied to the other photos in the same set.
instantX-research/InstantID: Identity-preserving generation from a single reference image, keeping the same person in a new picture. When you change the pose, scene, or style, the face still matches the reference photo, without first training a model for each person. One photo is enough, and you do not have to collect dozens of photos of the same person and train first. With more profile views and occlusion, identity drifts more easily.
libvips/libvips: A low-memory, high-speed image processing library. It processes large images as needed, and server-side thumbnails and format conversion often choose it instead of loading an entire high-resolution image into memory at once. When processing very large images it does not have to decode the whole image, which is why servers choose it. When a thumbnail service has many users, the memory advantage is more noticeable.
lllyasviel/stable-diffusion-webui-forge: A high-efficiency fork of Stable Diffusion WebUI, optimized for speed and newer models. The interface is close to the original WebUI, but it puts more weight on memory and on inference efficiency for newer-generation models. When GPU memory is tight, or you need to run a newer model, this fork is one to consider.
bmaltais/kohya_ss: A graphical interface for training LoRA and fine-tuning diffusion models. You prepare a set of images, train a small set of weights, then use them in WebUI or ComfyUI to lock in a character, an art style, or an object. Dataset organization and training parameters are both set in the graphical interface, so you do not have to rely only on the command line.
NVlabs/stylegan2: NVIDIA's StyleGAN2, which synthesizes high-resolution images with a generative adversarial network. It is known for high-quality synthesis of categories such as faces, and it is the base code for much later GAN editing and latent-space research. Latent vectors can be used for further editing experiments, and it is a common starting point for GAN face research.
Acly/krita-ai-diffusion: An AI drawing plugin for Krita that can inpaint and outpaint from a selection and a prompt. You stay inside the drawing software to edit the picture, without exporting it to another generation interface and pasting it back. Painters can use generation while staying inside Krita's layers and selections.
lllyasviel/IC-Light: A tool for controlling the lighting of a generated image. It can change light direction and environment while trying to keep the subject. It suits relighting an image so it looks placed in another scene, rather than resampling the whole picture. The subject is kept and only the light changes, which suits product photos and portraits when you change the ambient light.
yt-dlp/yt-dlp: A full-featured command-line audio and video downloader that can save video and audio from a large number of sites. You can choose the format, subtitles, and playlists, which suits people who need to archive or further process online video. It is updated frequently after sites change, and it is the mainstream choice for command-line downloading now. Playlists and subtitles can be saved in one pass.
obsproject/obs-studio: Free, open-source live streaming and screen recording software. It can mix screens, cameras, windows, and audio, then switch scenes, which suits livestreaming, teaching, and recording tutorials without buying separate capture software. Scenes can be arranged in advance and switched with one click during a stream. Teaching, livestreaming, and screen recording can share the same set of scenes.
calesthio/OpenMontage: An open-source agent video production system that produces video with multiple production pipelines and tools. You give it a production goal, and the system calls different steps to organize the material and a finished cut, rather than only offering an editing timeline. It suits people who want a finished video driven by a goal, rather than dragging the timeline piece by piece themselves.
remotion-dev/remotion: Make videos programmatically with React, for repeatable animation and templates. The picture is written as components, and when the data changes a new version can be rendered, which suits batch production of intros, charts, and social videos. The same video can be batch-rendered into many versions from data, for example one clip per person.
FFmpeg/FFmpeg: A core tool for audio and video, handling transcoding, cutting, streaming, and format conversion. Players, editing software, and website backends often call it for the actual decoding and encoding. When you write your own editing or streaming tool, the lower layer almost always calls it. Almost all audio and video software ends up calling it.
jellyfin/jellyfin: A free-software media system you can host yourself to organize and play video. You control the library, subtitles, and multiple clients, and it is used as a home media server without putting the library on a commercial platform. Several devices at home can play your own library, and you manage the accounts and metadata yourself.
mpv-player/mpv: A lightweight, high-quality command-line media player. It supports many formats and shaders, playback can be controlled by keyboard and scripts, and other interfaces often wrap it. Shaders and scripts can change the playback look, while the interface is usually wrapped separately. Configuration files can be synced to several computers.
ATH-MaaS/Pixelle-Video: An AI automatic short-video engine that goes from content all the way to a finished video. You can start from text or source material and let the pipeline handle the script, the visuals, and the output, shortening the time spent across many tools to make one short video. The short-video steps are chained together, so the script, the visuals, and the output do not each use a separate program.
hpcaitech/Open-Sora: An open-source video generation project aimed at lowering the barrier to high-quality text-to-video. It provides models and training and inference code so research and creative work can try text-to-video on open weights. If you want to change training or inference rather than only use a ready-made website, look at this open project.
Stability-AI/generative-models: Stability AI's generative model code, including image-to-video models such as Stable Video Diffusion. You can generate a short video starting from a single image, and it is also the official code collection for several of their generative models. Stable Video Diffusion for image-to-video and the code for the other generative models are both collected here.
HandBrake/HandBrake: An open-source video transcoding tool for compressing and converting to common formats. It has a graphical interface where you can choose device presets, which suits turning large files into versions that are easy to play or upload. Presets match common devices, so after conversion you can play or upload directly. When batch-converting, you can keep using the same preset.
k4yt3x/video2x: Video super-resolution and frame interpolation with machine learning. It can enlarge low-resolution video or raise the frame rate, so old footage and animation show less aliasing and stutter on a large screen. Upscaling and frame interpolation can be done separately, and both old animation and source video can be used. Models can be chosen separately for animation or live action.
bloc97/Anime4K: A real-time anime video upscaling algorithm that can improve quality during playback. It focuses on lines and flat color, which suits enlarging anime while you watch without first re-rendering the whole video offline. A player can apply it in real time, without first rendering a new file. Players such as mpv can attach this algorithm directly.
HBAI-Ltd/Toonflow-app: An open-source tool for short dramas and comic dramas, covering scripts, storyboards, characters and scenes, and image and video generation. The preproduction and visual steps a short video needs can move forward inside the same project. A short drama goes from script to picture, and the storyboards and characters in between can stay in the same project. Character settings can be carried into later storyboards.
KlingAIResearch/LivePortrait: Turns a single portrait into a moving portrait animation. You use one photo as the identity, then drive expressions and head movement, which suits portraits that talk or turn their head without first filming a video. A single portrait is enough, and the driving comes from another motion or expression clip.
Wan-Video/Wan2.2: An open-source large video generation model in Alibaba's Wan series. It can generate video conditioned on text or an image, with open weights and inference code, which makes it easier for research and further development to connect to your own pipeline. Open weights make it easy to connect it to your own editing or generation pipeline and try it.
lllyasviel/FramePack: Makes generation with video diffusion models more practical by lowering the memory pressure of long clips. It changes how frames are processed so a longer generation does not have to keep the state of every frame on the GPU at once. This way of handling frames becomes practically useful when the GPU cannot hold a long video.
storytold/filmcraft: Open-source nonlinear video editing software written from scratch in Rust. The direction is a local tool that can edit and organize a timeline, rather than wrapping another layer around an existing editing engine. It is for people who want to look at a timeline newly written in Rust, rather than another wrap around an existing editing core.
duixcom/Duix-Avatar: An open-source digital-human tool that can be used offline to generate talking-head videos and clone digital humans. mltframework/shotcut: Cross-platform open-source video editing software based on the MLT framework. Zulko/moviepy: A Python library for video editing, compositing, and basic effects. zai-org/CogVideo: A text- and image-to-video model project that includes CogVideo and CogVideoX. Tencent-Hunyuan/HunyuanVideo: Tencent Hunyuan's large open-source video generation framework. guoyww/AnimateDiff: Adds a temporal module to text-to-image models so they can generate short videos without retraining each one. Lightricks/LTX-Video: Lightricks' open-source video generation model and official code. magic-research/magic-animate: Temporally consistent character image animation with a diffusion model. gyroflow/gyroflow: Video stabilization using gyroscope data. OpenShot/openshot-qt: Cross-platform open-source video editing software with a fairly straightforward interface. genmoai/mochi: Genmo's open-source text-to-video model. AILab-CVC/VideoCrafter: A video diffusion model project for generating video with limited data. godotengine/godot: A cross-platform 2D and 3D game engine for real-time graphics, interaction, and animation. mrdoob/three.js: Create and render 3D scenes in the browser with JavaScript. pixijs/pixijs: A fast 2D WebGL rendering engine for interactive graphics and visual effects. pmndrs/react-three-fiber: A renderer for writing Three.js scenes in the React style. 3D objects can be written as components, and the picture updates when state changes, which makes it easier to put 3D into an existing React interface. BabylonJS/Babylon.js: A full-featured web 3D rendering and game engine. graphdeco-inria/gaussian-splatting: The original implementation of 3D Gaussian Splatting. blender/blender: The official Blender source code, covering modeling, animation, compositing, video editing, and rendering. google/filament: Google's real-time physically based rendering engine, usable on multiple platforms. bkaradzic/bgfx: A cross-graphics-API rendering library that lets your own engine target OpenGL, Direct3D, Vulkan, and Metal. NVlabs/instant-ngp: NVIDIA's instant neural graphics primitives, which greatly speed up training and rendering of NeRF-style scenes. playcanvas/engine: A web graphics engine built on WebGL, WebGPU, and glTF. It loads 3D scenes and runs interaction in the browser, and the editor ecosystem is built around this runtime core. Scenes load through glTF, and both the editor and the runtime are built around this core.
bulletphysics/bullet3: A real-time collision detection and physics library, commonly used in visual effects, games, and robotics. isl-org/Open3D: A modern 3D data processing library for point clouds, meshes, and visualization. Scan data can be filtered, registered, and reconstructed here, and both Python and C++ can call it. Cleaning and registration of scanned point clouds can be finished in Python and then visualized.
assimp/assimp: Reads more than forty 3D file formats into one data structure. alicevision/Meshroom: A node-based photogrammetry tool that reconstructs a 3D model from photos. nerfstudio-project/nerfstudio: A workbench for research on novel-view synthesis. NeRF and 3D Gaussian Splatting (splatfacto) can share the same data, training, and viewing tools. Switching methods does not require rewriting the whole set of scripts, which suits trying Gaussian reconstruction.
playcanvas/supersplat: A tool for editing 3D Gaussian splats in the browser. facebookresearch/pytorch3d: A component library for 3D deep learning with PyTorch. Meshes, cameras, and differentiable rendering can go into a training pipeline. carson-katri/dream-textures: Stable Diffusion built into Blender, so you can generate textures directly in the scene. opentoonz/opentoonz: A full-featured open-source 2D animation production program. PixarAnimationStudios/OpenUSD: Pixar's Universal Scene Description, for exchanging 3D scenes between different programs. cnr-isti-vclab/meshlab: An open-source mesh processing system for cleaning, repairing, and viewing 3D models. nerfstudio-project/gsplat: A CUDA-accelerated Gaussian Splatting rasterization library for research and integration. shader-slang/slang: A shading language that makes shaders easier to write and easier to compile across platforms. NatronGitHub/Natron: An open-source node-based compositing program, close in purpose to After Effects and Nuke. Masks, color grading, and effects are connected with nodes. mmp/pbrt-v4: Source code for the physically based ray tracer described in the fourth edition of Physically Based Rendering. AcademySoftwareFoundation/openvdb: A sparse volumetric data structure and toolset, a common format for smoke, fire, and clouds in visual effects. PixarAnimationStudios/OpenSubdiv: Pixar's open-source subdivision surface library. mitsuba-renderer/mitsuba3: A retargetable forward and inverse renderer for research-grade physically based rendering. AcademySoftwareFoundation/openexr: The high-dynamic-range EXR image format widely used in the film industry, and its reference implementation. AcademySoftwareFoundation/MaterialX: An open standard for exchanging material and look descriptions between different programs and renderers. AcademySoftwareFoundation/OpenColorIO: A color management framework for visual effects and animation. openbq-org/OpenBB: An open-source financial data platform for analysts, quant researchers, and AI agents. ranaroussi/yfinance: A Python library that downloads stock quotes and basic information from Yahoo Finance. A few lines of code can fetch historical prices and financial-statement summaries. mementum/backtrader: A Python library for backtesting trading strategies in an event-driven way. akfamily/akshare: An open-source financial data interface for fetching stocks, macro data, and other market data in Python. AI4Finance-Foundation/FinGPT: An open-source financial large language model for language tasks on financial text and markets. It can handle text such as news, reports, and sentiment. Open-Dev-Society/OpenStock: An open-source market platform for tracking prices, setting alerts, and viewing company information. bbfamily/abu: The Abu quantitative system. It covers stocks, options, futures, and Bitcoin, and it combines them with machine learning. UFund-Me/Qbot: An AI quantitative research and trading platform that can be deployed locally. waditu/tushare: A Python tool for fetching historical data on Chinese stocks. Quotes, financials, and some fundamentals can be downloaded through the interface. myhhub/stock: A Chinese-language stock tool that includes quotes, indicators, chart patterns, stock screening, backtesting, and automated trading. yutiansut/QUANTAXIS: A local quantitative system covering data, backtesting, simulation, and trading for stocks, futures, and options. shidenggui/easytrader: A stock trading interface for Tonghuashun, miniQMT, and Xueqiu. It can also follow simulated portfolios. mudler/LocalAI: An open-source local AI engine that can run language models, vision, speech, images, and video on your own machine. taichi-dev/taichi: A language and compiler for writing high-performance GPU programs in Python. stefan-jansen/machine-learning-for-tradi: Code for the third edition of Machine Learning for Trading. deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness: The official agent harness from DeepSeek, whose architecture treats everything as a plugin. NousResearch/hermes-agent: An autonomous agent from Nous Research that writes experience it has used into skills and remembers who you are. khoj-ai/khoj: A self-hosted personal AI second brain. It finds answers on the web and in your documents, and you can also build custom agents, schedule automation, and do deep research. ssloy/tinyrenderer: A short computer graphics course that writes a small renderer from scratch in C++. questdb/questdb: A high-performance open-source time-series database for storing and querying timestamped data such as market data. camenduru/stable-diffusion-webui-colab: A set of Google Colab notebooks for running Stable Diffusion WebUI on Colab. stablyai/orca: An agent IDE for desktop and phone. It runs several coding agents, such as Codex and Claude Code, side by side, each in its own git worktree. You can use your own subscription and follow progress in the terminal, on a remote machine, and on a phone.
divamgupta/diffusionbee-stable-diffusion: A desktop app for running Stable Diffusion locally on an M1 Mac, with one-click install, so you do not have to assemble the dependencies yourself. leejet/stable-diffusion.cpp: An inference program that runs diffusion models in pure C/C++, with support for SD, Flux, Wan, and others. It does not need a full Python deep-learning framework. JerBouma/FinanceToolkit: A Python library for transparent financial analysis. It can pull financial statements, compute ratios, and compare factors. ssloy/tinyraytracer: A short ray-tracing course that writes a small renderer from scratch in C++. As you follow the lessons, you implement ray-scene intersection yourself. getopenscreen/openscreen: An open-source screen recorder for product demo videos. It supports Windows, macOS, and Linux, with GPU acceleration and no watermark or subscription. Clips stay on your own machine. It suits people who need to produce demos and do not want a closed-source recording tool.

siyuan-note/siyuan: A self-hosted, privacy-first knowledge workspace. Notes are stored as Markdown on your own machine, and people and AI agents can organize and search them together. It is for a personal knowledge base, rather than handing notes to an outside service.

cloneofsimo/lora: An early implementation that fine-tunes diffusion models quickly with low-rank adaptation. Training only a small part of the weights can add a new style or subject to Stable Diffusion. It suits people who want to fine-tune it themselves without retraining the whole model.
hudson-and-thames/mlfinlab: A toolkit for financial machine learning. It covers common steps in labeling, features, portfolios, and backtesting, so you can study how a strategy is trained on data. darkzOGx/youtube-automation-agent: A self-hosted video agent. It writes a script, voiceover, and visuals from a topic, publishes only after you approve, and then adjusts the next video from the data. hku-mars/FAST-LIVO2: LiDAR-inertial-visual odometry from the MaRS Lab at the University of Hong Kong. nexu-io/html-video: A tool that renders HTML, CSS, and data into an MP4 on your own computer. A coding assistant can ask it to produce a video. advimman/lama: LaMa uses Fourier convolutions for large-area image inpainting, so a large masked region can still be filled from the surrounding texture. geekyutao/Inpaint-Anything: One click outlines an object, and segmentation and inpainting models then remove it, fill it, or replace it from text. You do not paint the mask yourself. Images, video, and 3D scenes each have a corresponding workflow, which suits clearing away pedestrians and clutter or swapping one object for another. Selection and redrawing are separate, so the whole image is not changed together.
lxfater/inpaint-web: Image inpainting and upscaling in the browser, running locally with WebGPU and WASM, so images do not have to be uploaded. Paint over a flaw and it is filled from the surroundings, and you can upscale at the same time. It suits people who do not want to install Python first and want the files to stay on their own computer. Opening the page is enough to use it.
Bing-su/adetailer: A Stable Diffusion WebUI extension that uses a detection model to outline a region automatically and then redraws it locally, mostly faces and hands by default. If the details break after an image is generated, you can redraw only that spot without painting a mask by hand, while the composition and the other areas stay as they were. Faces and fingers are the parts most often repaired this way.
lkwq007/stablediffusion-infinity: Outpainting on an infinite canvas with Stable Diffusion. You start from one image and keep generating toward the edges, so the picture can keep extending without deciding the final size in advance. This is outpainting more than filling holes, and it suits people who want to widen a composition or lengthen a scene. The canvas has no fixed boundary.
JiahuiYu/generative_inpainting: The official code for DeepFill v1 and v2, which fills irregular holes with contextual attention and gated convolution. The model looks at the image around the hole to decide what to fill in, rather than smearing nearby pixels together. These are classic implementations from CVPR 2018 and ICCV 2019, and they are now often used as research baselines for comparison.
knazeri/edge-connect: It first predicts the edges of the missing region, then fills color and texture along those lines. Building and object outlines are easier to keep, so the fill does not become a structureless patch of color. This is structure-guided inpainting from ICCV 2019. Lines are fixed first and color is filled afterward, so hard-edged objects look more natural.
andreas128/RePaint: Image inpainting with a denoising diffusion model, without training a new network just to fill holes. An existing diffusion model can repeatedly redraw the gap according to the mask, while known regions stay as they were. CVPR 2022. If you already have a generative model, you can use it to repair the image without training a separate inpainting network.
TencentARC/BrushNet: A pluggable diffusion inpainting model that uses separate dual branches for the mask and the original image. It can attach to an existing text-to-image model and redraw the brushed region without retraining the whole base model. ECCV 2024. If you want to keep the original diffusion model, adding one inpainting branch is enough.
scraed/LanPaint: A training-free inpainting sampler that can be applied to existing diffusion and rectified-flow models. Inside the mask it takes a few extra steps before denoising, spending more compute for a more stable fill, and it also supports replacing a local region from text. It has a ComfyUI node. The method itself is a sampling paper, not only a node package. TMLR.
open-mmlab/PowerPaint: One model handles several kinds of image inpainting at once: inserting an object from text, removing an object, outpainting, and guidance by shape. Changing the task prompt is enough, so you do not install a separate model for removal and for redrawing. ECCV 2024. The same weights can change purpose, so removing and adding objects does not require swapping weights.
fenglinglwb/MAT: Large-hole image inpainting with a Transformer. The mask affects attention, so the model knows where to generate and where to keep. When a large area is missing, distant texture can be aligned, instead of relying only on a few pixels at the edge of the hole. It suits gaps so large that ordinary convolution cannot see the whole context.
Picsart-AI-Research/MI-GAN: A mobile-oriented image-inpainting baseline that uses distillation and reparameterization to compress the model so it can run on a mobile device. The emphasis is that the image still looks clear after an object is removed, without relying on a desktop-class GPU. ICCV 2023. If you want erasure on a phone, this is more practical than a large desktop model.
DQiaole/ZITS_inpainting: Structure-enhanced image inpainting from CVPR 2022. It first restores lines and edges step by step, then fills texture with mask position encoding, so buildings and regular objects do not end up warped. When the gap contains straight lines or outlines, the structure is restored first and the color is filled afterward.
lyndonzheng/Pluralistic-Inpainting: The same gap can be filled in several ways that are all plausible, rather than returning only one answer. When the hole is large and more than one content would be reasonable, you can pick the one that fits the picture best. This is pluralistic image completion from CVPR 2019. It does not force every image to have only one way of being filled.
researchmm/AOT-GAN-for-Inpainting: High-resolution image inpainting with aggregated contextual transformations, looking around the gap at several scales together. It aligns texture in a large image more easily than single-scale convolution, and it suits high-resolution photos that need a region filled. This is an image-inpainting program from TVCG 2023. When filling a high-resolution image, fine and coarse scales are used together.
open-mmlab/mmagic: OpenMMLab's toolbox for generation and creation, used for text-to-image, image and video restoration, upscaling, and editing. Models and training scripts already have ready interfaces, and inpainting is only one of the tasks. If you want to try several generative models in the same library, you can switch among them here without installing a separate stack for each model.
vllm-project/vllm-omni: vLLM's multimodal inference framework for running image, audio, and video generation models efficiently. The focus is deployment and throughput, not a canvas or an editing interface. You can start a service on your own machine and let other programs call these models. It suits a backend that needs to serve several modalities at once.
GuanYixuan/pyJianYingDraft: A Python tool that generates Jianying drafts. You can place video, images, a timeline, and effects in code, then export the draft into Jianying and keep editing, which is a way to build an automatic editing pipeline. The CapCut version is developed in another repository. It suits people who need to produce videos in batches and still want drafts that can be edited again.
NVlabs/neuralangelo: NVIDIA's high-fidelity neural surface reconstruction, for recovering a detailed 3D surface from photos, with contours that fit the object more closely than earlier neural radiance fields. This is the official code from CVPR 2023. The output is a surface mesh, not a texture or a video. It suits reconstructing an object's shape from real footage.
dcajasn/Riskfolio-Lib: A Python library for portfolio optimization. You can compute the efficient frontier, risk, and weights, and compare different allocations. It is a research tool, not a program that automatically places orders with a broker. It suits asset allocation and risk analysis, and placing orders requires you to connect a trading interface separately.
vladmandic/sdnext: SD.Next is a local web interface for running diffusion models to generate and edit images, and it can also handle video and write descriptions. It supports many GPUs and CPUs, and the model can be swapped. It suits people who want a Stable Diffusion workbench that keeps being updated, rather than relying only on an older interface.
AbdBarho/stable-diffusion-webui-docker: An install package for running the Stable Diffusion web interface with Docker. You can open a ready-made interface and generate images without building a Python environment yourself. The repository itself is not a model. It packages an existing interface as a container. It suits people who want to run an image-generation service on their own machine quickly.
antgroup/echomimic_v2: Ant Group's half-body portrait animation, which uses audio to drive speech and body movement. You can give it an audio clip and a reference image, and it generates a video with matched lips and pose. CVPR 2025. The focus is portrait performance, not general video editing or text-to-video. It suits talking-head videos and virtual humans.
Tencent-Hunyuan/HunyuanVideo-1.5: Tencent Hunyuan's lightweight video generation model, which can make a video from text or from an image. The focus is a small model that is easy to run while keeping a watchable picture. The official code and the notes on the weights are in this repository. It suits people who want to try text-to-video on their own machine without deploying an extremely large model first.
quantopian/alphalens: A Python library for judging how accurate a stock-selection factor is. You can look at how a signal relates to later returns, grouped returns, and turnover, and then decide whether it is worth taking into a backtest. It is a research tool, not an order-placing program. Quantopian has shut down, but the code can still be used for factor analysis.
civitai/civitai: Civitai's open-source program for running a community site that shares models, textual inversions, and LoRAs. You can browse, upload, and download weights trained by other people, rather than generating images from text here. It suits people who want to host a model-sharing site themselves, or see how the platform is built.
AbdullahAlfaraj/Auto-Photoshop-StableDif: A Photoshop plugin for calling Stable Diffusion directly inside Photoshop to generate and edit images. The backend can be Automatic1111, and it can also connect to ComfyUI. You stay with the original layers and tools, without exporting the image and pasting it back. The plugin itself is not a model.
tmoroney/auto-subs: A tool for making subtitles on your own computer, so the audio and video do not have to be uploaded. It can be used on its own, and it can also connect to DaVinci Resolve, Premiere, and After Effects. It supports multilingual transcription and translation, and it can tell who is speaking. It suits people who need local subtitles and want them to go straight into editing software.
shashankvemuri/Finance: A Python toolkit for quantitative research. You can pull market data, compute technical indicators, screen stocks, backtest strategies, and optimize a portfolio. The examples are a starting point, and you change the rules yourself. It is a research tool, not a program that automatically places orders with a broker. It suits people who want to try a strategy starting from the data.
zvtvz/zvt: A modular quantitative framework for pulling market data, building factors, and backtesting in one place. Stocks are the main subject, and it also covers cryptocurrency data. You can swap the data source and the strategy without writing a separate stack for each market. It suits people who want to study different markets with the same program. You have to connect trade execution yourself.
fudan-generative-vision/champ: Portrait animation guided by 3D parameters, which can turn one portrait into a stable video according to the motion. ECCV 2024. The focus is keeping the person's motion and appearance consistent, not general text-to-video. It suits research on character animation from a single photo. The official code follows the paper.
FlashML-org/FreeVideo: An inference engine for running MiniMax H3 video generation on a home computer, with VRAM that can be as low as 8GB. It chooses precision according to the GPU and loads the weights in batches, so the whole model does not have to sit in VRAM at once. The interface is a ComfyUI workspace, with launchers for Windows, Mac, and Linux as well. The model is an existing one, and this repository runs it locally.
wheresryan22/anatomy: A Claude skill for turning a concept into an interactive isometric mechanical diagram. The output is SVG, WebGL, or 3D, with the parts broken down finely. It asks a coding assistant to build an object you can understand, rather than only returning a passage of text. It can also be used in Codex and OpenCode.
rddmwmddr/android-ad-cleaner: A tool for turning off ads, hot-search prompts, and promotional notifications on Chinese-brand Android phones. It does not need root, and the changes can be undone. You can plug in the phone and click through a desktop program, or hand it to an AI agent to run all at once. It suits people who want to clear system ads without flashing the phone.
andyhuo520/digital-human-koubo: An agent skill that generates a digital-human talking-head video from one photo and one script. It calls Renoise's service for lip sync and packaging, rather than training a model from scratch on your machine. It suits people who want to hand the job to Claude Code or Codex to produce a talking-head video.
Jakeschincariol/day-trader-skill: A set of Claude skills that scan charts, follow the news, and replay old price paths using free public data. Before you place an order, you can look back at how a pattern moved afterward. It is a research and review tool, not a broker order-placing program, and it does not guarantee that you will make money.
storytold/effectcraft: Open-source motion-graphics and compositing software written in Rust. You can build frames and effects on a timeline without relying on a subscription compositing tool. The program is written by the author, and it suits people who want a lightweight compositor. Compositing and editing a finished film are two different jobs.
Arekejoker/qwen21-nsfw-pose-skill: An agent skill for generating images from a pose with Qwen-Image inside ComfyUI. The recipe includes prompts, an adult-oriented LoRA, and more than a hundred 3D poses. It suits people who want a coding assistant to follow fixed steps and produce the images. The content is adult-oriented, not a general illustration tool.
patch-gg/anymove: It captures the motion of any creature from a video, fits that motion onto a skeleton, and exports GLB. The same frame has two camera views, used to align the joints. It can also be used as an agent skill and handed to a coding assistant to run. It suits games and 3D characters that need motion and do not have a motion-capture studio.
deepopen-com/deepopen-3d-webs: From one reference image and a prompt, it generates a previewable 3D scene along a camera path. The browser can play color, depth, and a Gaussian point cloud. The site is started with Docker. It suits people who want to go from one photo to a replayable scene, rather than ending with only a still image.
wide-trace/open-higgsfield: An open-source image and video studio that calls several existing models with one prompt. You have to bring your own platform keys. The studio itself is not a model. It suits people who want to try different image and video models on the same screen without being locked to a single website.
Gen-Verse/RSI-Anything: Research on using world models for recursive self-improvement. The system first predicts the next outcome, then learns from the interaction, and then changes the next decision. The repository follows the paper. It suits seeing how a world model takes part in a decision, not a game you can play right away.
kaomei/stickman-video-director: An open-source pipeline that turns a script or a topic into a stick-figure animation. Picture, voiceover, subtitles, and sound effects can be assembled in one pass. It suits faceless channels, without drawing every frame yourself. The output is a finished video, not only a storyboard. The finished video stays on your computer.
jundizhou/easy-stock: A desktop investment-research workbench for A-shares. You can watch quotes, research individual stocks, and review after the close, then ask an AI to organize the evidence. It is an analysis tool, not a program that automatically places orders with a broker. It suits people who want to do that review on their own machine. You make the judgment yourself.
scenario-labs/blender-plugin: Scenario's Blender add-on, which can generate images, video, 3D models, and PBR materials in the viewport. It also opens a local MCP so an agent can call these features. It requires Blender 5.0 or newer. Generation calls their service, and it is not a model built into Blender.
mylxsw/aidea: A mobile app written in Flutter that puts several large language models and image-generation models in one program. You can chat and also generate images, and the model interface can be swapped. The program is open source. It suits people who want to connect different models on a phone with their own keys.
t3dotgg/tstack: A collection of the agent skills Theo uses every day, cleaned up so other people can use them. They can run in Claude Code and Codex. When T3 Code is present they use its features, and when it is not they fall back to the native tools. It suits people who want a ready set of everyday development skills without writing skills from scratch.
DenisSergeevitch/ex-ussr-kinship-researc: A genealogy skill for AI agents, specifically for looking up kinship records from the former Soviet Union, the Soviet Union, and the Russian Empire. It reads church registers and civil, military, and exile archives, and it separates what is confirmed from what is inferred. It suits people who need to trace a family and want every item to keep its source.
lexmount/moli: A headless browser written in Rust for an AI agent to control web pages. The emphasis is that it is light, fast, and highly compatible. You can open pages and carry out actions in an environment with no window. It suits people who want their own agent to browse the web without relying on a heavy browser.
OpenMOSS/MOSS-Image: OpenMOSS's image model with 5 billion parameters, strong at text inside images and at layout. It can be fine-tuned. The official code and the notes on the weights are here. It suits image generation that needs clearly rendered text, not a canvas application. You have to download the model yourself and then run it.
obsidianmd/pele: Obsidian's official Mermaid diagram renderer, which turns diagrams into SVG. The program is small, runs synchronously, and has no runtime dependencies, and its colors follow CSS variables. It supports the diagram types in Mermaid 12. It suits producing a flowchart quickly, not doing video compositing.
openfilm/openfilm: An open-source AI video agent. You can turn the coding assistant you are already using into a video assistant, and after it finishes there is still an editor for changing the frames it generated. It suits people who want to build a video through conversation and then edit it section by section, rather than only receiving a finished piece. Generation and editing stay in the same workflow.
mexicat/pdoom-video: A music video rendered by a program, with subtitles timed to the song. Each frame is determined by the song's time, so the browser preview matches the exported 1080p or 4K. It is a work for this song, not a general video-making tool. You can render it again on your own machine.
Noniv/web-ocean: A WebGPU ocean-rendering demo. A single HTML file can open it in Chrome. It has FFT waves, foam, sunlight, and a sunset sky. You can fly the camera freely. There is no game engine. It suits looking at how a real-time water surface is written, not a 3D software package.
11cafe/jaaz: An open-source multimodal creation assistant that can run locally, for design and generation, positioned as an alternative to tools like Canva. Privacy comes first. It suits people who want to create images and text on their own machine without handing drafts to a subscription website. Drafts and conversations can both stay on the machine.
Picsart-AI-Research/Text2Video-Zero: It uses a text-to-image diffusion model to make video in a zero-shot way. Without training a new model for video, it can generate short clips from text or from an image. This is the official code for an ICCV 2023 oral. It suits research into how an image model can be extended to video.
lightly-ai/lightly: A Python self-supervised learning library for learning representations on images, and it also includes latent world models. You can train on unlabeled images and then use the representations for downstream tasks. It suits visual pretraining, not a video-making program or a trading program.
luigifreda/pyslam: Visual SLAM in a mix of Python and C++. It supports monocular, stereo, and RGB-D, can estimate how the camera moves, and also includes Gaussian splatting and semantic segmentation. It suits research on localization and reconstruction. It is a full pipeline, not only a point-cloud viewer.
xai-org/grok-build: SpaceXAI's terminal coding agent. The full-screen interface can view a project, edit files, and run commands. It can also run with no interface, or be embedded in an editor through the Agent Client Protocol. The program is written in Rust and is synced from their main repository. It suits handing development work to the terminal without opening a web chat window.
Jakeschincariol/replica-skill: Eleven Claude skills for taking apart an app's workflow and having an agent build one again. They require that only the functionality be rebuilt, without copying the code, the logo, or the copy. They can be installed as a plugin in Claude Code. It suits people who want to use a skill pack to try a similar product, not a ready-made application.
morganlinton/BeautifulRust: Rust skills for coding agents. One teaches idiomatic writing, one handles review and points out which rule applies, and one ports programs from C, Python, and other languages to Rust. There is also a clippy configuration that can be placed in CI. It suits people who want an agent to follow the official style when writing Rust, without pasting a guide themselves every time.
sirioberati/Genjustsu-Open-Source-Workfl: A local interface for replacing a person or an object in a video. It prepares depth, a SAM mask, and a face mesh, then hands them to Seedance to generate, and on export it keeps the original audio for the whole clip. You need to connect the Enhancor API separately. It suits character replacement, and it is not a video model trained by this project.
glanderness/BeefTV: A local-first AI video workbench that connects assets, models, and agents on a canvas. The desktop version can run on your own machine, from storyboard changes through to a finished film. Commercial use of the new code requires a separate license. It suits people who want to build a video on a canvas, and it is not a video model trained from scratch.
Vincentwei1021/anything2explainer: A Claude Code and Codex skill that uses Remotion to turn a topic into an explainer short, with voiceover, subtitles, and a chapter bar. Every frame is drawn by code, not by a generative model. Both Chinese and English work. The tool itself is under a non-commercial license. It suits using an agent to produce an explainer, rather than receiving a ready-made video.
yanliudesign/mono-color-skill: An image skill for producing monochrome or two-color editorial images, such as posters, zines, and portraits. The default is one main color plus a small accent, and the background can be white paper or warm paper. It is style guidance, not a new image model. It suits images with a printed look, not ordinary full-color generation.
hi3d-official/Hi3Dv1.0: Hi3D's official inference program. It uses a reference image to refine a coarse mesh into higher-resolution geometry. The base is Sparc3D, and the weights are on Hugging Face. The repository has inference and no training code. It suits adding detail to a coarse model you already have, not generating from scratch from a single image.
arnegiacomo/fugleramme: It uses a local sound model to recognize birds in the garden, then displays them as nineteenth-century hand-drawn illustrations. It can sit on e-paper, a television, or a Raspberry Pi. Recognition is done on your own machine. Whichever species is heard, that picture is swapped in. It suits setting up a bird picture frame, not video compositing or a 3D scene.
absolute-quantum/cats-blender-plugin: A Blender add-on for tidying models from MMD, Mixamo, DAZ, and similar sources, then sending them to VRChat. One click can reduce the polygon count, set up lip sync and eye tracking, and merge bones. It suits shortening the steps for uploading a virtual character, and it is not a render engine.
AI4Finance-Foundation/FinRL-Trading: Quantitative trading infrastructure in the FinRL series, called FinRL-X. It gathers data, strategies, backtesting, and broker order placement into one weight interface. There is a PyPI package and a paper. It suits people who want to go from researching a strategy to simulated order placement, rather than only a reinforcement-learning tutorial library.
simonlin1212/TradingAgents-astock: A multi-agent investment-research framework that adapts TradingAgents for A-shares. Seven analysts debate using data such as the dragon-tiger list and lock-up expirations. It can be installed with pip, and it is positioned as research and teaching. It suits trying multi-role investment research, not an automatic order-placing trading program.
airbnb/lottie-web: Airbnb's web Lottie player renders JSON exported from After Effects through Bodymovin. It only plays the animation in a browser. The motion is authored in AE or another tool, then exported.
airbnb/lottie-android: Airbnb's Android Lottie player renders animations exported from After Effects through Bodymovin. It is a native playback component, so the file is authored in AE or another tool first.
airbnb/lottie-ios: Airbnb's iOS Lottie player renders vector animations exported from After Effects on iPhone and iPad. It is a playback component, so the motion is authored in AE and then exported.
Tencent/libpag: Tencent's PAG renderer turns After Effects animations into a portable file and plays them on mobile, web, and desktop. PAG and Lottie JSON are different formats. It is a player, not a full editor or compositor.
LottieFiles/dotlottie-web: LottieFiles' dotLottie web player uses Rust and WebAssembly to play compressed Lottie files. It plays After Effects exports in the browser. It is a player, not a timeline editor.
lottie-react-native/lottie-react-native: A React Native wrapper around the native Lottie players, used to play After Effects exports inside an app. It is a framework binding, so the animation is still authored in AE.
Samsung/rlottie: Samsung's standalone C++ library plays Lottie JSON exported from After Effects through Bodymovin, without a browser. It is a playback engine, not an editor or compositor.
alyssaxuu/motionity: A timeline motion-graphics editor that runs in the browser, for cutting animation, type, images, and effects, then exporting a clip. It is an editor, not a node compositor. After Effects is not required; a browser is enough.
tixl3d/tixl: TiXL is a desktop app for realtime motion graphics, built with nodes and a timeline. Parameter changes show up immediately. It is a standalone program, not an After Effects plugin.
mojs/mojs: A motion-graphics toolbelt for the web. Code draws shapes, tweens, timelines, and burst effects in the browser. The motion is written in code, without opening AE. It is a front-end library, not an After Effects plugin or a video editor.
astrofox-io/astrofox: Astrofox is a motion-graphics program that turns an audio track into visuals that follow the beat and the spectrum, then exports a clip. It is built for music visualization, not general editing or compositing, and it does not need After Effects.
motion-canvas/motion-canvas: A framework for motion graphics written in TypeScript. You lay out a timeline and tweens in code, then render a video. It is code-driven motion, not an After Effects plugin, and AE is not required.
theatre-js/theatre: A motion-design editor for the web. You adjust animation on a visual timeline and hand it to front-end code to play. It is a motion-design tool, not After Effects or a video editor, and AE is not required.
rezoo/movis: A Python library for video, motion graphics, and shader art. You stack layers and render from code. It is a library, not an After Effects plugin, and the machine does not need AE.
ManimCommunity/manim: The community Python framework for mathematical animation. It draws formulas and geometry step by step and renders a teaching film. It makes teaching videos, not commercial After Effects comps, and AE is not required.
inlife/nexrender: Data-driven render automation for After Effects. It swaps text and footage in batches and outputs the renders. After Effects must be installed on the machine, because nexrender asks AE to render.
RxLaboratory/Duik: Duik Ángela is a rigging and character-animation tool that runs inside After Effects, adding skeletons and controllers to layers. It is an AE panel, not a standalone 3D app, so After Effects must be installed.
ntsc-rs/ntsc-rs: A Rust VHS and analog-TV look. It runs as a standalone app and also as a plugin for After Effects, Premiere, and OpenFX. It is an effect, not a full compositor.
baku89/ISF4AE: An After Effects plugin that runs GLSL written as ISF, so a custom shader becomes an effect inside AE. It is a plugin, not a transition pack, and After Effects must be installed.
JacquesLucke/animation_nodes: A Blender add-on that builds motion graphics with nodes, driving objects, time, and effects procedurally. It runs in Blender, not as an After Effects plugin, so AE is not required.
toadstorm/MOPS: Motion Operators for Houdini, a node toolkit for motion graphics and procedural animation. It runs in Houdini, not on After Effects layers, and the machine does not need AE.
mrachinskiy/commotion: A Blender add-on for motion graphics, used to build procedural animation and effects inside Blender. It is not an After Effects plugin, and After Effects does not need to be installed.
xvrh/lottie-flutter: A pure-Dart Flutter player for Lottie animations exported from After Effects. It is a playback widget, not a video editor, so the animation is authored in AE and then exported.
thorvg/thorvg: A production C++ vector engine that renders SVG and Lottie, meant to be embedded in other programs. It is a graphics library, not After Effects and not a video editor, and AE is not required.
